The two cellular process pathways consistently enriched (KEGG over-representation analysis, adjusted p < 0.05) across all three quorum-sensing mutant strains (97, 98, 99) vs wildtype (strain 1) for the significantly downregulated genes (p<0.05, log2FoldChange < -1.5) are:

1. **Quorum sensing (KEGG map `pau02024`)**
2. **Biofilm formation – Pseudomonas aeruginosa (KEGG map `pau02025`)**

Both lie under the KEGG BRITE category **Cellular Processes → Cellular community – prokaryotes** (the two organism-annotated "cellular process" pathways for pau that pass the all-three-strain filter).

Key data-anchored results (background = 5828 detected PA14 genes, identical across the three files; ORA = one-sided hypergeometric + Benjamini–Hochberg):

| **02024 Quorum sensing** | 10/17 | 4.4e-12 / 8.8e-12 | 13/17 | 1.9e-17 / 3.8e-17 | 15/17 | 2.9e-16 / 7.9e-16 | **YES** |
| **02025 Biofilm formation – P. aeruginosa** | 11/18 | 1.9e-13 / 5.1e-13 | 16/18 | 2.6e-23 / 1.1e-22 | 17/18 | 1.8e-19 / 7.2e-19 | **YES** |

Data-anchored negative control: the flagellar cluster (PA14_36470–36920) and the che/mot chemotaxis genes are strongly downregulated only in strains 98 (24/28, 4/10) and 99 (28/28, 4/10), whereas in strain 97 they are essentially unchanged (e.g., PA14_36590 lfc −0.10, p=0.70; PA14_37610 lfc −0.07, p=0.66), giving 0 enriched-member overlap → p=1.0 in strain 97. Therefore flagellar assembly and bacterial chemotaxis are NOT consistently enriched across all three strains, and the two passing Cellular Processes pathways are Quorum sensing and Biofilm formation – P. aeruginosa, which are instead anchored on the loci that ARE downregulated in all three strains (e.g., 10/11 of the 59 genes downregulated in all three mutants fall inside the reconstructed 02024/02025 member sets, chiefly the shared QS-regulon operons PA14_55790–55940 and PA14_06720–06860).
